newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Far East power workers to strike till paid.
newsitem.headline: Russian Far East power workers to strike till paid.

text.p: Striking power workers in Russia's Far East vowed on Wednesday not to give up until they are paid, and threatened to mount a general strike across the region.
Dozens of their colleagues entered their third week of a hunger protest. Households and industry in the key port city of Vladivostok are spending large parts of every day without power.

More than 10,000 power workers out of the region's 17,000 went on strike on Monday, demanding payment of wage arrears estimated by union leaders at 130 billion roubles ($24.1 million). Many workers were last paid in April.

"The strike will go on until all back wages to power workers, including those for September, have been paid," Olga Kochegureva, a senior official at the power workers' trade union in the far eastern Primorsky region, told Reuters.

The union at the region's electricity utility Dalenergo has appealed to workers in other industries to join their strike, but has had no response so far. It plans to call for a general strike on October 10 if the dispute is not settled by then.
Power workers have cut off electricity supplies to industry and residential areas in vast parts of the region, about a third of whose population of over two million live in Vladivostok.

Residents of the regional capital and Russia's main Pacific port, who had been using candles and kerosene stoves in frequent black-outs for weeks before the power workers' strike, seemed to be less affected than industrial companies.

The power workers' union is trying to shift the main burden of black-outs onto local industrial plants, especially those who owe Dalenergo money. As a result, ordinary residents, who are already inured to power cuts, have found life slightly easier.
Directors of some industrial plants in the highly militarised region, which was closed to foreigners in Soviet times, say they are being seriously affected by the strike, but have not elaborated.
Many firms say they can not clear debts to the power company because they themselves are owed money by the state.
Some 130 workers at Primorsky hydroelectric station continued their hunger strike into the 15th day on Wednesday, demanding back pay of around 30 billion roubles.
Fifty emaciated hunger strikers have already been taken to hospital.
But regional governor Yevgeny Nazdratenko appears unruffled by the crippling energy crisis.
The regional assembly on Wednesday bowed to his wishes and called off a referendum Nazdratenko had originally planned for this Sunday as a way of seeking a popular vote of confidence.
Nazdratenko had called the referendum, whose results would not have been binding on the governor, after a presidential commission sent from Moscow blamed him for failing to avert the energy crisis.
